findings.title: Take phase 7 (WSL2 guest collector) out of v1 and drop the 'moves after phase 2' rule; v1 shows the VM as one opaque workload and measures its share from its own data
findings.evidence: docs/13-build-list.md:11-35 no ingest component; :82 'POST /sessions the only write'; docs/15:35-37 P7 is a gate only; docs/15:45 decision rule; docs/16:81 R05 'The ingest API accepts a second collector'; docs/17:79; docs/10:11; docs/03:61 doctor 'WSL2 VM holds 3% of CPU time'. learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking (re-fetched): 'By default, WSL uses a NAT ... based architecture'; Linux to Windows 'you need to use the IP address of your host machine'; but Windows to Linux 'you can access it from a Windows app ... using localhost', and mirrored mode (Windows 11 22H2+, opt-in) lets you 'Connect to Windows servers from within Linux using the localhost address 127.0.0.1'. sqlite.org/wal.html (re-fetched): 'All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.'
findings.impact: P7 has no component, route, schema or transport, and its conditional move depends on a working-day measurement with no denominator (B-measurement#15). Deferring loses the per-process view inside WSL, which v1 shows as one opaque workload anyway.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead: delete P7 (docs/15:35-37); docs/15:45 'Not in version 1. The VM is an opaque workload; doctor reports its share of busy CPU time from v1 data. A guest collector is designed after v1 if that share is large.' Delete docs/17:79 ingest sentence, :264 sentence and the WSL item in :268; mark R05's ingest part not in v1; add 'a collector inside WSL2 or Docker Desktop' to docs/13 'Not in version 1'; drop 'in phase 7' at docs/10:11; docs/01:29 '8 phases'. State the reason as 'no transport is designed', not 'none can obey rule 3', and record the candidate transports for later: host pulls over WSL localhost forwarding, or guest-written JSON files with atomic rename.
findings.cost: About 10 lines across docs/15, 17, 13, 10, 16, 01, plus the same passages in docs/brief.html. No code.
findings.decision_question: Defer the WSL2 guest collector after v1 and let v1's opaque-VM workload measure the share (recommended), or keep P7 and its conditional move, which first needs a designed transport (host pull over localhost forwarding, mirrored mode, or a non-SQLite file drop)?
findings.verification: Re-read every cited line; all match. Re-fetched the three Microsoft pages and sqlite.org/wal.html; quotes are present. Correction: the lead's 'P7 has no design that obeys fixed rule 3' is overstated. Microsoft's networking page shows a Windows program reaching a WSL service via localhost under the default NAT mode (host-pull keeps the host API on loopback), and mirrored mode gives guest-to-host 127.0.0.1. The WAL rule rules out only a live SQLite file shared across /mnt/c, not JSON files written with atomic rename like the run files. The 'We recommend against working across operating systems with your files' quote is a performance recommendation ('unless you have a specific reason'), not a correctness rule. The case for deferral rests on no component, no transport and an undefined decision rule, and that holds. Another option, not tested: run the Linux build standalone inside WSL (the compare-versions table lists systemd support for WSL 2), with its own store and no transport. Severity stays medium.

findings.title: Build tagged runs first (launcher, holder, run file, `run`, `cost --run`, load generator) as phase 1, before the poller and store
findings.evidence: docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:83 'This decides whether tagged workloads can be exact, which is the centre of the design' (unverified on Windows). docs/13-build-list.md:23-24 launcher and providers.group in P2. docs/17:66 'A tagged run is therefore accounted for even if the collector was not running'; docs/05:52; docs/06:17 runs/*.json written by the Launcher. src/submeter/attribution/rules.py:196-216: aggregate() sums polled per-process values; kernel_workloads only sets the label. docs/review/probes/a-linux/cgroup_totals.out.txt: 'cpu.stat usage_usec of the group: 10.677 s (-0.01%)'.
findings.impact: If Job Object facts (nesting, totals after exit, name lifetime) surface in P2, P1's models, raw schema and run-file contract reopen. The owner's main question waits behind P1's soak although it needs no collector.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15 and docs/17:268-270: new P1 'Tagged runs' = component 13 with its detached holder, the final-totals part of 14, the run file, `submeter run`, `submeter cost --run` over run files, the load generator; gate = 500 sub-second children within 2% of the load generator's own accounting, final totals survive exit, `run` returns with the exit code while left-behind processes are still counted. Old P1 becomes P2; live group reading and re-attach move with attribution. docs/13:23-24 phase cells. Settle the run file's life (docs/06:17 'Until read', F-consistency#5) in the same edit.
findings.cost: Two phase paragraphs in docs/15 and docs/17, two cells in docs/13, plus brief.html copies. No code.
findings.decision_question: Reorder so that tagged runs are phase 1 and the poller and store phase 2 (recommended), or keep the brief's order and rely on the P0 Job Object probe (H8) to retire the risk first?
findings.verification: Re-read every cited line and the probe output (not re-run: it spawns CPU load, and other verifiers are timing). I found no dependency of the launcher on the collector or store: it writes its own run file and baseline core, config and redact code already exist. Downgraded from high to medium: reordering makes no number wrong and fails no gate. The risk is rework later, and H8's owner-run Job Object probe in P0 retires most of that risk before P1 whatever the order. Caveats: `cost --run` over run files differs from docs/17:127 (cost reads stored summaries in history), so it is an interim reader; the new gate's reference must be independent of the kernel figure (G-buildability#1), as the lead proposes.

findings.title: Cut hot and cold sets: read every process every tick, slow only the costly fields, and make 2 s the default active interval
findings.evidence: Re-ran docs/review/probes/b-measurement/hot_cold_sampler.py (output identical): A 'credited 30.0 CPU-s of 94.8 (32%), processes 'started' 1620, 'exited' 1620 (truth: 0 and 0)'; B 'cores p50 0.49, p95 11.62 (truth 1.58 both), capacity 8'. Re-ran model_tables.py (identical): 'whole tick + raw store 36.0 ms ... 1s 3.60% (over) 5s 0.72% (ok)'; '10% of 300 processes hot: ... 1s 0.68%'. docs/review/probes/verify-9/scope_evidence.out.txt: direct /proc 2s 1.80%; psutil fallback 95.1 ms gives 2s 4.75%, 5s 1.90% (over). reconcile_terms.out.txt:3 'the smallest use that can be seen in one second is 1% of a core'; getconf CLK_TCK = 100. docs/17:71 bulk call returns counters 'for every process'. docs/08:61,63,65; config.py:84,86; sampler.py:104 hot_keys.
findings.impact: As specified, hot and cold sets either credit about a third of CPU time and invent 1,620 starts and exits a minute, or show more cores than the machine has. The only in-budget figure at 1 s comes from the variant that is wrong.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead: docs/17:71 'Read cumulative counters for every process every tick; read USS or PSS, command line and working folder on the slow cadence.' docs/17:170-174 and docs/08:61,63,65: active_interval 2s; delete cold_interval and hot_cpu_threshold. docs/04:8, docs/05:12,45 (not :84), docs/13:17, docs/17:238, R02 fix text: drop hot and cold sets. config.py: remove the two fields and their types (lines 49, 67, 84, 86); sampler.py: remove hot_keys; tests/test_baseline.py:130,138,223 follow. docs/08 explorer and the brief.html calculator: drop the cold-interval input. State that 2 s is in budget only with a direct reader; on the psutil fallback the guard lengthens the interval.
findings.cost: About 12 document lines, about 20 code lines and about 6 test lines removed, plus the brief.html text and its calculator script.
findings.decision_question: Cut hot and cold sets and move the default active interval from 1 s to 2 s (recommended; 1.80% of a core per 300 processes with a direct /proc reader on Linux), or keep 1 s and schedule the per-process-interval sampler redesign (B-measurement#3 option 2)?
findings.verification: I re-ran both probes; their output was identical. I recomputed the arithmetic in my own probe. Corrections: (1) a 0.5% threshold is unresolvable only on Linux (USER_HZ 100); Windows CPU times are in 100 ns units. (2) The 452 processes are this review machine's count (ground/platform-check.txt:8), not the owner's. (3) The 2 s budget holds only for a direct reader: the psutil fallback reaches 4.75% at 2 s and needs at least 3.2 s active and 9.5 s idle, and Windows is unmeasured. (4) docs/05:84 does not exist (the file has 80 lines; the hot set is at :12 and :45). (5) The code cut also touches tests. Going to 2 s lowers polled capture of short-lived children (modelled 29% to 15%; measured 2.9% at about 1.13 s), which widens B-measurement#10's reconciliation gap but does not change its verdict. Severity stays high: the specified feature fails the 2% reconciliation and capacity under real load.

findings.evidence: docs/04:38 'so an agent can ask what it is costing'; docs/15:33 P6 gate 'an agent can retrieve its own cost for a session'; docs/17:197 'every command accepts --json with a stable schema'; docs/13:69-83 has no cost or run route; AGENTS.md:46 three runtime dependencies; uv.lock: 'name = "mcp"' count 0; config.py:196-198 Api.mcp_enabled. Agents run git, rg and pytest: docs/02:91-92, docs/16:55 (R01).

P6 gate (docs/15:31-33, docs/17:274): 'an agent retrieves its own run's cost with `submeter cost --run "$SUBMETER_RUN" --json`, and the output holds no command line'; the launcher sets SUBMETER_RUN in the child's environment. Also edit docs/04:38, docs/05:27,50, docs/08:107,125, docs/17:53,148,193 and brief.html; remove Api.mcp_enabled.

findings.decision_question: Defer the MCP server after v1 and serve agents through `submeter cost --json` (recommended), or keep it in v1 with an approved SDK or a hand-written stdio server?
findings.verification: I re-read the cited lines. docs/17:60 does not name git, rg or pytest; docs/02:91-92 and R01 do, so the claim holds with a corrected citation. The lead's edit list misses MCP at docs/05:27,50, docs/08:125, docs/17:53,148,193,245,274 and brief.html, so the cost is about 14 lines, not 6. Asking 'what am I costing' mid-run needs live group totals through MCP or through the CLI alike, so there is no MCP-only capability. SUBMETER_RUN is a new contract (from G), not yet in the docs. Setting a child's environment does not conflict with docs/17:96, which bans reading other processes' environments.

findings.title: Cut the minute tier: keep raw (48 h) and hourly (kept); leak check on raw workload rows, baselines (if kept) on hourly
findings.evidence: docs/06-storage.md:64-65: the only minute-tier readers are the leak check (2 to 48 h back, inside raw retention) and the baseline (14 d). Re-ran docs/review/probes/h-scope/minute_tier_reach.py (identical): 'windows answered by the minute tier: 11 of 21'; 'minute tier is chosen for spans over 33.3333 min and up to 33.3 h'; 2 d, 7 d and 30 d windows already come from 'hour/3600s'. growth.py:26-33 thins to 300 points; rollup.py:100-110 roll_up takes any width_s; rollup.py:9-10 docstring builds hourly 'from minute buckets' against docs/17:123 'from raw data'.
findings.impact: A third file kind with its own writer, retention, migration window and membership rules serves no job's acceptance test, and several storage leads (C-storage#2, #9, #11, #12; F-consistency#15) exist partly because of it.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead: docs/06:11-19,48-67,111, docs/17:105,154,156, docs/04:21, docs/05:19,35,48, docs/13:20,40, docs/08:81; R23's fix text; query.py: inside raw retention answer from raw merged to wider steps, else hourly; files.py: remove minute_file and expired_minute; tests/test_baseline.py:319,429-432,454 follow.
findings.cost: About 15 document lines, about 30 code lines and about 8 test lines, plus brief.html. Close to the fix-now limit.
findings.decision_question: Go to two tiers, raw and hourly (recommended; lost: windows of 34 min to 33 h that start 2 to 30 days back fall from 1-minute to 1-hour resolution, and per-core detail beyond 48 h), or keep the minute tier?
findings.verification: I re-ran the probe; its output was identical. I read query.py's choose_tier and confirmed the tier logic. Added caveats: (1) windows of 1 to 24 h ending now, answered today from the minute tier, would come from raw merged at query time (24 h at 1 s is 86,400 rows per series). This is untimed, and it matters mainly for the dashboard, which H11 defers. (2) Under disk pressure raw may fall to 24 h (docs/17:141); that still covers the 2 h leak acceptance but not the 48 h lookback. (3) docs/06:90 keeps per-core load 'in the raw and minute tiers', so per-core detail older than 48 h is lost. (4) R23's fix wording must change. No acceptance line needs 1-minute data older than 48 h. Severity stays medium.

findings.title: Defer baseline anomaly and slow growth; v1's trend job is leak detection, diff and hourly history; the Windows I/O verdict must stop depending on an undefined baseline
findings.evidence: docs/08:89-90 slow_growth.window 7d, baseline.learning_period 7d; docs/07:35 days 1-7 raise nothing. docs/07:99 Windows I/O-bound 'Disk queue and latency above baseline'; docs/03:32 'run queue 2.3 per core baseline 0.4'. docs/06:81-82 baseline inputs are CPU time and growth memory only; docs/06:93 disk latency feeds only 'I/O verdict'. docs/01:18 job 3 acceptance names only the leak. grep -rni spike src: only growth.py:4 docstring. docs/06:15 hourly kept.
findings.impact: Two detectors needing weeks of real data would be built against fixtures with known defects (B-measurement#8, #9; F-consistency#10). Job 2's Windows I/O-bound verdict cannot fire, because its system-level baseline is defined nowhere.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead: docs/13:27 v1 detectors = leak and process count; baseline anomaly, slow growth, spike and swap storm go to 'Not in version 1' or get a one-sentence rule each; edit docs/04:30, docs/08:89-92, docs/17:155-156,158, docs/15:21 (drop 'a leak too slow for the hourly check'); docs/07:99 uses absolute disk queue and latency thresholds; docs/03:32 drop 'baseline 0.4'. The ranking of jobs at docs/17:15 is a separate owner decision.
findings.cost: About 12 document lines in 6 files, plus brief.html. No code removed.
findings.decision_question: Defer baseline anomaly and slow growth (recommended), and separately: rank the jobs attribution > diagnosis > trends for future cuts, or keep 'equal weight'?
findings.verification: I re-read every cited line and confirmed that no system-metric baseline exists anywhere in docs. Correction to 'nothing is lost': the stored data is kept, but job 3's automatic regression finding (docs/17:19 'leaks and regressions'; docs/07:29 baseline = 'a regression against the usual range') goes. In v1, regressions are found by hand with `diff` and the hourly history. R34's fix (slow growth) is undone for v1, so R34 must be marked deferred. Changing 'three jobs of equal weight' alters the owner's own priority statement, so it is split out as its own decision.

findings.title: Make phase 0 three decision probes on the owner's machine plus CI; remove the VRAM drift, WSL working-day and 'doctor correct on both' items
findings.evidence: docs/15:9 and docs/17:268 (doctor 'correct on both', VRAM check, WSL share, full-sample cost). docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners (re-fetched): 'Windows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled'; GPUs only on larger runners. measure/snapshot_cost.out.txt: psutil 74.6 ms per 300 vs direct /proc 7.5 ms. docs/11-language.md:21 switching rule; windows-priorities.md:83 Job Objects unverified.
findings.impact: As written, a builder cannot close P0: doctor has no oracle, the VRAM check needs a GPU, and the WSL share needs a working day. Meanwhile the three facts that change v1's design (holder design, language and interval, how autostart installs) are tested late or never.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead: docs/15:9 and docs/17:268. P0 = (1) the four checks and platform_check.py on the owner's machine as the signed-in standard user; (2) CI on both OSes for portable tests; (3) three owner-run probes with saved output: Job Object create, nest, totals after exit, reopen by name after the creator exits; a bulk-snapshot prototype at the owner's process count; per-user autostart without elevation. The gate is that each probe's output is saved and its dependent choice recorded.
findings.cost: Two paragraphs, plus brief.html. Three probe scripts of 100 to 200 lines each, written by the builder.
findings.decision_question: Replace P0's VRAM, WSL-day and full-matrix items with the three decision probes on the owner's machine (recommended), or keep P0 as written?
findings.verification: I re-fetched the GitHub page and the quote is present. I re-read the cited lines and the measure output. Condition: removing the VRAM and WSL items is right only if H9 and H1 are accepted. If either is rejected, its measurement moves to that phase and is not dropped. The autostart probe rests on suspected leads (G-buildability#13, D-privacy#13), which is the reason to probe it. 'Doctor grows with each provider' leaves doctor's own correctness without a pass criterion until each provider phase defines one.

findings.title: Trim phase 5 to GPU load by engine (plus adapter-level VRAM); defer per-process VRAM, connections, battery level and Linux temperatures
findings.evidence: docs/06:88 'VRAM ... GPU verdict. Leak checks only once validated'; docs/06:89 'Connections ... Workload table'; docs/07:100 GPU-bound 'Ruled out when: VRAM is full, which is reported separately'; docs/07:95-102 uses no connections, battery or temperature; docs/10:14; docs/13:16 frequency in component 06 (P1) vs docs/13:33 'throttling' in 23; docs/17:273 'Hardware you do not have is tested from recorded fixtures'; docs/17:29 priority 1.
findings.impact: A phase of providers is built mostly from synthetic fixtures for metrics no job reads, and one P0 item (VRAM drift) needs owner hardware for a metric v1 will not use for leak checks.
findings.proposed_change: Component 23 = 'GPU load by engine type, machine-wide and per process, busiest as headline, and adapter VRAM used and total'. docs/13 'Not in version 1': per-process VRAM, connections, battery level (keep the on-battery flag that docs/08:71 needs), temperatures. Edit docs/15:9,27-29, docs/01:23, docs/04:10, docs/17:85-90,176, docs/08:68-70. Alternatively, delete the VRAM rule-out at docs/07:100.
findings.cost: About 10 document lines and 2 setting fields, plus brief.html.
findings.decision_question: Keep only GPU load and adapter VRAM from the extra telemetry in v1 (recommended), or keep per-process VRAM, connections, battery and temperatures?
findings.verification: I re-read every cited line, and my probe printed the docs/07 GPU-bound row and the docs/06 VRAM catalogue row. Correction: the lead's refutation says only the workload table and an untrusted gauge use these metrics, but docs/07:100's rule-out and docs/06:88 make VRAM an input to the GPU verdict, a job-2 class. Cutting all VRAM leaves that rule-out unevaluable. Adapter-level VRAM is a different source from the per-process counter that R16 distrusts, so keep it, or drop the rule-out. thermal_interval also covers power: the on-battery flag must still be read for the cadence multiplier (docs/08:71).

findings.title: Shrink the settings surface: settings read at start (reload = restart), no profiles, no per-session interval; 13 of the 42 rows go with other cuts
findings.evidence: Hot reload: docs/13:12, docs/17:187, docs/08:5. Session interval: docs/08:74, docs/17:190. Profiles: docs/08:117, docs/17:180, config.py:277-306, cli.py:43,47,111,117, tests/test_baseline.py:122-137. verify-9/scope_evidence.out.txt: 'docs/08 sampling rows 60-72: 13; other rows 80-108: 29', 'rows named as cut by other findings and present: 13 of 13'. sampler.py:50-51 first snapshot returns None.
findings.impact: Hot reload and session overrides each need a control channel (G-buildability#5) and mid-run epoch rules the brief lacks; profile selection is unspecified (F-consistency#11) and unselected profiles are not validated (E-baseline#17).
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:187-190: 'Settings are read when a program starts. `submeter config reload` restarts the collector and server; the restart starts a new epoch if settings, rules, version or hardware differ.' Delete the session interval override (docs/08:74, docs/17:190) and profiles (docs/08:117, docs/17:180); per-machine settings come from --file or SUBMETER_HOME; docs/13:12 drop 'hot-reloads'; remove profile handling from config.py, cli.py and its test.
findings.cost: About 8 document lines; about 20 config.py lines, 6 cli.py lines and 16 test lines removed; plus brief.html.
findings.decision_question: Read settings only at start and drop profiles and the per-session interval in v1 (recommended; lost: a change without restart, one file shared across machines, and 250 ms benchmark sessions), or keep all three and specify the control channel?
findings.verification: Row counts and cited lines confirmed by my probe and by re-reading. Two overclaims: (1) 'only the start of a program begins an epoch' does not settle F-consistency#4. Adaptive cadence and the overhead guard still change the interval mid-run (docs/08:60,72), and docs/17:130 makes sampling intervals part of an epoch, so that rule still needs its own ruling. (2) Reload by restart still needs a safe stop channel (G-buildability#5; D-privacy#15 warns about pid-based stop), though `daemon stop` needs one anyway. The removal also touches cli.py and tests, which the lead's cost leaves out; the total is still under 50 lines.

findings.title: Make v1 CLI-first: defer the HTTP API, WebSocket and dashboard; charts come from `submeter report`; add a findings command and a file path for session markers
findings.evidence: docs/01:7 (`submeter cost`), :12 (`submeter why`), :17 ('History view, findings feed, `submeter diff`'). docs/15:25 is the only dashboard gate. src/submeter/cli.py:21-27 imports attribution, sampler, provider and store.files directly; docs/05:50 routes the CLI through the API. verify-9/scope_evidence.out.txt: 'docs/13 commands: 13: daemon, run, top, why, cost, diff, session, report, export, config, rules, store, doctor', 'a command that lists findings: False', 'POST /sessions the only write': True.
findings.impact: Two components, a phase, v1's only network listener, a token system and four or more unapproved dependencies serve none of the three jobs' acceptance tests, and they carry the critical rule-3 lead (D-privacy#11) and about seven other leads.
findings.proposed_change: As the lead (docs/13:30-31,64,69-83; docs/15:23-25 to a 'Report' phase with a self-contained HTML file and a meta CSP; docs/01:22, docs/04:35-38, docs/05:44-50, docs/17:21,38-39,148,195-214,254,272; docs/08:107-108). Add: (1) a `submeter findings` command (or a findings section in `why` and `report`) so job 3's leak flag has a surface; (2) `session start|stop` writes a session marker file with atomic rename, which the server reads, replacing POST /sessions.
findings.cost: About 30 document lines in 7 files plus the two additions (about 6 lines), plus brief.html. No code.
findings.decision_question: Ship v1 as collector + background server + CLI + static HTML report, with the live dashboard and API in v1.1 (recommended), or keep the dashboard and API in v1 and take the token, Host/Origin, asset and dependency fixes from D, F and G?
findings.verification: I re-read the cited lines and cli.py, and my probe listed the commands. Two gaps the lead missed: (1) no CLI command lists findings, and job 3's surface is 'findings feed' (docs/01:17), so with the dashboard gone the leak flag that job 3 accepts on has nowhere to appear; (2) session markers travel only by POST /sessions (docs/13:82), so with no listener `session start|stop` needs a file path. Both are small. The lead's 'each job names a CLI command too' holds fully only for jobs 1 and 2. Citation docs/01:16 should be :17. Deferring the listener strengthens fixed rule 3.

findings.title: Build one OS's platform layer in v1; the other OS runs polled with portable CI
findings.evidence: docs/13:14-15 (04 Windows bulk, 05 Linux procfs), :23-24 (Job Object and cgroup). docs/17:266 'you can only run one OS yourself'. prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:3 'my Windows 11 work computer'. GitHub runners page (re-fetched): 'Windows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled'. a-linux/cgroup_scope.out.txt: 'passing memory down while this process is in it: refused (Device or resource busy)', 'exit code 1: Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'; cgroup_totals.out.txt 'io.stat NO'. windows-priorities.md:100 'Linux needs its own pass later ... None of that code exists yet.' Lead counts: A-linux 16, A-windows 12.
findings.impact: Every platform phase carries two kernel-accounting designs and two gates. On Windows the second can be checked only in CI as administrator, so a gate passed there can fail on the owner's machine as a standard user.
findings.proposed_change: docs/01:25 and docs/17:21: v1 builds the platform layer (kernel accounting, launcher and holder, system counters, autostart) for one OS. The other OS runs polled: `submeter run` reports tagged runs unavailable and runs the command polled, and its CI runs the portable tests. Cheaper middle: keep that OS's bulk reader if it is the measured-cheap /proc reader (component 05). Mark the deferred halves of 04/05, 13 and 14 'after v1'; gates name one OS.
findings.cost: About 8 document lines, plus brief.html. No code; provider interfaces stay.
findings.decision_question: Which OS gets the v1 platform layer: Windows, where builds run per prompts/01:3 (recommended), or Linux, where kernel accounting is already shown exact (-0.01%)? Or keep both OSes in v1? Accepting a one-OS layer means job 1's 'tagged within 2% of the kernel' does not hold on the other OS in v1.
findings.verification: I re-fetched the GitHub quote and re-read the cited lines and probe outputs (cgroup probes not re-run: they create cgroups and spawn load). Caveat on the cheaper alternative: the psutil provider is over budget at the default cadences (whole tick + store 95.1 ms per 300 processes: 1 s 9.51%, 2 s 4.75%, 5 s 1.90%; verify-9 probe). On psutil alone, the second OS runs with the guard at 3.2 s or more active and 9.5 s or more idle (Linux figures), so 'keeps the psutil provider' needs that stated, or the cheap /proc reader (7.5 to 15.5 ms) kept. AGENTS.md:47 (code passes on both) still holds through portable CI. Severity stays high: the second OS's gates cannot be verified under the owner's conditions.

findings.title: Defer desktop notifications; in v1 alert rules raise findings that the CLI and report show
findings.evidence: docs/15:47 'Dashboard and desktop notifications only'; docs/13:32 'dashboard and desktop delivery'; pyproject dependencies pydantic, psutil, typer; AGENTS.md:46; docs/08:98-99 quiet_hours, channels; docs/13:41 history has a `finding` table; docs/01:8,13,18 no acceptance line names a notification.

findings.title: The floor of version 1: what must not be cut, and the six-phase list that results
findings.evidence: docs/01:8 job 1 (parts within 2%, tagged within 2% of kernel); docs/01:13 job 2 (verdict under 2 s, Inconclusive); docs/01:18 job 3 (50 MB/h leak flagged within 2 h, warm-up not); docs/17:29-30 priorities 1 and 2; docs/17:98 reconciliation over the four fixed buckets; AGENTS.md:41 redaction before storage; R01, R07, R26.
findings.impact: Without a stated floor, cuts could reach a part a job's acceptance depends on.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15 once the cuts are ruled: P0 decision probes and CI; P1 tagged runs; P2 collector and raw store (with the baseline attribution and its four fixed buckets, so reconciliation can be tested); P3 attribution rules, history, sessions, hourly rollup, retention, budget, backups; P4 verdict and `why`, leak, process count, diff, alert findings; P5 report and GPU load. Add to the floor: a CLI surface for findings (job 3); a session-marker path that needs no API; adapter VRAM, or a rewritten GPU-bound rule-out (job 2). Matching lines in docs/17:268-275.
findings.cost: One rewritten phase list in docs/15, the matching docs/17 lines, docs/01:29 counts, plus brief.html.
findings.decision_question: Adopt this floor, with the three additions, as the line no cut may cross, and the six-phase list once the individual cuts are ruled (recommended)? Or rule each cut first and derive the list afterwards?
findings.verification: I traced each floor item to docs/01 acceptance lines, docs/17 priorities or AGENTS.md. Three gaps found by the H9 and H11 checks are added above. The P2/P3 split puts reconciliation before attribution, but reconciliation needs the four fixed buckets (docs/17:98), so P2 must use the baseline attribution (rules.py) or G-buildability#4's cross-phase dependency comes back.
